lines.text: The deorbit burn.
We were coming *down.*
I'm a flight engineer. I knew where the thruster breakers were.
Mara read me the panel. I pulled them by hand. One. Two. Three. Four.
The engines stopped.
Silence. Then Mara laughed. Then I did.
We were in a lower orbit. Low enough to fall in a few weeks. High enough to last five days.
Five days. That was all we needed.
Day three sixty-one. Three sixty-two. Three sixty-three.
Water: under two percent. Half rations. We talked out loud all day, just because we could.
Day three hundred sixty-five.
A capsule docked at the front port.
And someone knocked. Three times.
Rule one. Not for anyone. Not even for me.
I opened it anyway.
Bright light. Cold air. A face I knew.
It was Hale.
He looked at the two of us, and said: you followed rule two.
And then: I'm sorry. It took me a year.
Two seats. We went home.
Mara saw rain. I saw my mother.
Larkspur Orbital was taken apart in court, with Inés's recordings and Hale's testimony.
Project SOLO was shut down. No one will ever be told they're alone up there again.
For one year, I lived alone on a space station.
That's what they told me.
I was never alone.
Neither was *she.*
